entries.name: Slice
entries.what_it_is: Face open to path, producing right curvature. The classic amateur version starts left or straight and curves hard right.

causes.text: Out-to-in path with face open to that path.
causes.signal: ball starts left of target then curves right.

causes.text: Face open to target and to path.
causes.signal: ball starts right and curves further right.

causes.text: Heel strike via gear effect.
causes.signal: face marking toward the heel, ball speed down, curve present even when path feels neutral.

causes.text: Early extension pushing the hands out and the path left.
causes.signal: often paired with thin or heel contact.

fixes.text: Strengthen the grip so the face sits more closed. Highest-leverage single change, because face dominates start direction.
fixes.kind_reason: matches generate.py's structural grip rule: grip strength or how the hands sit on the grip

fixes.text: Feel the clubhead exit right of the target through impact.

entries.name: Pull-slice
entries.what_it_is: Face closed to target but path even further left, so the face is open relative to the path. Starts left, curves right. One of the most common amateur ball flights.

causes.text: Steep out-to-in path with a face that is closed to target but open to path.
causes.signal: divot points left, ball starts left.

causes.text: Over-the-top transition from the top.
causes.signal: shoulders opening early, steep angle of attack.

fixes.text: Shallow the path so it works more right, while keeping face awareness so the ball does not simply become a pull.
fixes.kind_reason: starts with 'shallow', a cue for the swing itself

fixes.text: Feel the trail elbow drop in front of the hip in transition.

differentials.what_separates_them: Check where it started: left means a pull-slice, right means a push-slice, straight means a slice.
Check the curve. A pull goes straight left with no curve, and a pull-slice curves back right.

entries.name: Push-slice
entries.what_it_is: Face open to target with path also right of target but face open relative to it. Starts right, curves further right. The biggest single-shot miss in golf by total offline distance.

causes.text: In-to-out path with the face badly open to it.
causes.signal: divot points right, ball starts right.

causes.text: Very late or absent face rotation.

fixes.text: Rotate the face closed earlier through impact.
fixes.kind_reason: starts with 'rotate', a cue for the swing itself

fixes.text: Check grip strength first, since this pattern usually has a weak grip underneath it.

entries.name: Fat / heavy / chunk
entries.what_it_is: Low point behind the ball, so the club contacts ground first and loses energy.

causes.signal: divot starts well behind the ball, finish balance poor.

causes.text: Early release or casting from the top.
causes.signal: divot shallow and long, high ball flight, distance loss.

causes.text: Body rotation stalling so the arms release early.

causes.text: Poor arc height control, independent of low point position.

entries.name: Ball below feet
entries.what_it_is: A lie that promotes a fade or slice for every golfer, regardless of swing. With lofted clubs, much of the effect comes from the slope tilting the clubface so its loft points right of the target. That effect grows with loft, so it is large with wedges and short irons and small with a driver or fairway wood. With long clubs the curve comes mainly from the bent-over posture, which makes a full turn through the ball harder and can leave the face open.

fixes.text: Aim left to allow for the curve.
fixes.kind_reason: starts with 'aim', done before the swing: aim, ball position, stance, where the club is held, tee height, club choice or a check

fixes.text: Flex your knees more at address to get down to the ball.

fixes.text: Hold the club near the end of the grip, since the ball is further from you.

fixes.text: Take one more club, as the lie costs distance.
fixes.kind_reason: starts with 'take', done before the swing: aim, ball position, stance, where the club is held, tee height, club choice or a check

fixes.text: Stay at the same height through the ball rather than rising up. Standing up is the common error and causes thin and topped shots.
fixes.kind_reason: starts with 'stay', a cue for the swing itself

notes.label: Why it matters

entries.name: Downhill lie
entries.what_it_is: The slope reduces effective loft, producing lower launch and more run. Also the hardest lie to make clean contact from. The ground behind the ball is higher than the ball, so the club tends to catch the slope first unless the swing follows the slope down, and trying to lift the ball to avoid that causes thin contact.

entries.name: Bunker shot left short
entries.what_it_is: Insufficient distance from a greenside bunker despite escaping.

causes.text: Entry point too far behind the ball, taking too much sand.
causes.signal: deep divot in the sand, distance well short.

causes.text: Deceleration through the sand.
causes.signal: short follow through.

causes.text: Sand heavier or wetter than expected.
causes.signal: conditions, and a pattern across the round.

causes.text: Face not open enough, so the club digs rather than sliding.

fixes.text: Enter the sand a consistent distance behind the ball and accelerate through.
fixes.kind_reason: starts with 'enter', a cue for the swing itself

fixes.text: Commit to a full finish, since bunker shots need more speed than they feel like they should.
fixes.kind_reason: starts with 'commit', a cue for the swing itself

entries.name: Good shot, nothing to diagnose
entries.what_it_is: A shot that did what you intended. Includes a deliberate shape that came off, since a fade you meant is not a miss.

notes.label: Why it needs an entry
notes.text: Without one, a query describing a good shot returns the nearest fault, and the tool invents a problem that is not there. Diagnosing a good shot is worse than saying nothing, because it teaches you to change something that is working.

notes.label: Correct response
notes.text: Log it and move on. No fix, no swing thought. If `intended_shape` was set and the shot matched it, that is worth recording as a success rather than a neutral event.

notes.label: Watch for
notes.text: A good outcome from a bad decision is still a bad decision. If the shot came off but the strategy flag fired, log the decision quality separately. See S003 and R001.
